limitations_and_boundaries: Possibility that elimination of postsynaptic material by microglia might occur in other brain regions, at other developmental stages, or at low frequency not detected in these experiments.
Immunofluorescent colocalization of postsynaptic proteins with microglia should be interpreted with caution due to potential non-phagocytic membrane exchange.
Anecdotal electron microscopy data on spine head filopodia converging to form MSBs should be interpreted with caution.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

Light sheet fluorescence microscopy of microglia-synapse interactions in developing organotypic hippocampal cultures

methods.name: Light sheet live imaging
methods.protocol_description: Live imaging of hippocampal slice cultures (DIV10-19) using Zeiss Z1 light sheet microscope at 35°C and 5% CO2. Imaging performed for 2-3 hours with 60x/NA1 water-immersion objective, lateral pixel size 130 nm, axial step 480 nm. For two-color imaging, 488 and 561 nm lasers used simultaneously; for three-color imaging, fast switching between 488/561 and 638 nm lasers.

methods.name: CLEM sample preparation and FIB-SEM
methods.protocol_description: Mice perfused with 2% PFA/2.5% glutaraldehyde at P15. 60 µm vibratome sections stained with DAPI. ROIs imaged by confocal microscopy, then laser-etched. Sections processed for FIB-SEM: postfixed with OsO4, stained with uranyl acetate and lead aspartate, embedded in Durcupan. MicroCT used for correlation. FIB-SEM imaging at 5 nm pixel size, 8 nm slice thickness.

methods.name: Analysis of microglia-phagocytic capacity
methods.protocol_description: C57BL/6J mice perfused with 4% PFA at P8, P15, P28, P40. Coronal 50 µm sections immunostained for CD68 and Iba1. Confocal imaging at 48 nm lateral pixel size, 130 nm axial step. 3D reconstruction of Iba1-positive microglia using Imaris, CD68 signal intensity measured per cell.
